html:
Khama III was chief of the Bangwato, the largest of the Tswana states, from 1875 until his death in 1923, and is the best known of the chiefs who founded Botswana.

A Christian convert, he banned alcohol, ended some old rites and ruled firmly from Shoshong and later Serowe. He welcomed British protection in 1885 against the Boers and the Ndebele.

In 1895, when Britain planned to hand the protectorate to Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company, Khama travelled to Britain with two other chiefs. Their tour of churches and meetings won public support, and the colonial secretary kept the territory under the crown. Without that journey, Botswana might have shared Rhodesia's fate. His grandson Seretse Khama became the first president.
sum: Khama III was chief of the Bangwato, the largest of the Tswana states, from 1875 until his death in 1923, and is the best known of the chiefs who founded Botswana.
